title: Add FP8 attention kernel path behind runtime flag and wire into registry/dispatch
creator: Hiro Tanaka
description:
Goal
Integrate the FP8 attention kernel implementation into the serving runtime behind a runtime flag, register it in the kernel registry, and ensure dispatch + fallback behavior is safe and measurable. This ticket is intentionally scoped to wiring + guardrails (not full heuristic policy, which is in ENG-7430 / ADR-019).

Why
We need a controlled mechanism to run apples-to-apples benchmark comparisons and canary rollout without customer impact. FP8 attention can materially improve decode/prefill throughput on H100 (and potentially A100 depending on shape + kernel availability), but the integration must be gated and observable.

Scope
- Add a new attention kernel variant entry in the kernel registry for FP8 (per supported GPU arch).
- Implement dispatch path selection behind a runtime flag (default OFF).
- Enforce shape/support guardrails (head_dim alignment, hidden-size constraints, max seq-len regime if required by kernel).
- Add correctness test coverage + a small perf smoke hook for benchmark harness.
- Ensure metrics tagging includes kernel-mode dimension so perf canary can compare baseline vs FP8.

Non-goals
- Final auto-selection heuristics for default enablement (tracked in ENG-7430 / ADR-019).
- Scheduler tuning (tracked in scheduling workstream).
- INT8 matmul integration (ENG-7424).

Proposed implementation
1) Feature flags
- Add runtime flag: runtime.kernels.attention.fp8.enabled (bool, default false)
- Add optional per-model override allowlist: runtime.kernels.attention.fp8.model_allowlist (comma-separated model IDs) to support safe canary.
- Add optional kill-switch for known-bad shapes: runtime.kernels.attention.fp8.disable_shapes (pattern list) for rapid mitigation.

2) Kernel registry
- New registry key: attention.fp8.v1 (name TBD in code) with metadata:
  - supported_arch: sm90 (H100) initially; sm80 (A100) only if kernel path is stable
  - supported_head_dims: 64/128 only (initially)
  - supported_dtypes: fp8_e4m3fn (weights/activations per kernel contract)
  - kv_cache_layout requirements (alignment + stride)
- Registry entry should expose “is_supported(shape, device)” predicate used by dispatch.

3) Dispatch + fallback
- Dispatch should attempt FP8 attention only if:
  - flag enabled AND model in allowlist (if allowlist non-empty)
  - device supports FP8 path (sm90 initially)
  - shape passes guardrails
  - kv-cache layout contract is satisfied (or can be converted without extra copy)
- Otherwise fallback to baseline attention kernel (existing path).
- If FP8 kernel returns an error at runtime (unexpected), catch + fallback once per process with rate-limited logging (avoid log spam + perf impact).

4) Correctness + testing
- Add unit test(s) that validate output parity within tolerance vs baseline for:
  - short-context prefill (seq 32/128)
  - decode step (seq 1 incremental)
  - representative head_dim 64 and 128 shapes
- Add negative tests verifying fallback triggers for unsupported shapes.
- Integrate with CI smoke bench (if available in this cycle) by providing minimal test entrypoints.

5) Observability
- Emit metric tag kernel_mode=fp8_attention when path is selected.
- Emit counter: attention_fp8_fallback_total with reason tag (unsupported_arch | unsupported_shape | kv_cache_layout | runtime_error | allowlist_miss).
- Ensure TTFT/TPOT breakdown is unaffected by additional instrumentation (no debug logging on hot path).

Acceptance criteria
- Runtime builds with FP8 attention path compiled in and disabled by default.
- Toggling runtime.kernels.attention.fp8.enabled enables FP8 path for supported shapes on H100.
- Guardrails reliably force fallback for unsupported shapes/architectures without crashing.
- Correctness tests added and passing in CI.
- Metrics include kernel_mode dimension and fallback reason counter.
- Bench harness can exercise the flag without code changes (see ENG-7422).

Rollout notes
- Default OFF for runtime-1.22.0.
- Canary plan: enable for 1-2 internal cohorts / regions on a single model ID first, verify TTFT/TPOT + error rate + fallback counters, then expand.
- Any TTFT regression > threshold triggers rollback (see ENG-7426 / perf canary profiles).

Owners / reviewers
- Owner: Grace Kim
- Reviewers: Yuki Sato (registry/dispatch), Marcus Reed (perf suite implications), Rafael Mendes (canary safety), Rina Kobayashi (harness integration expectations)

Open questions (resolved in comments)
- Exact FP8 format support (E4M3 vs E5M2) and whether we need runtime config knobs.
- A100 support: keep behind same flag but require explicit allowlist and “unsupported_arch” fallback by default until we validate kernels.
